trial_court: Family Court-cum-III Additional District Judge, Warangal, O.P.No.44 of 2007
facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties was performed on 20.02.2002. Appellant filed a petition under Section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 seeking dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty.

legal_principles.principle: Cruelty is not defined in any statute, and the concept of cruelty differs from person to person depending upon his upbringing, level of sensitivity, educational, family and cultural background, financial position, social status, customs, traditions, religious beliefs, human values and their value system.
legal_principles.held: The concept of cruelty differs from person to person depending upon his upbringing, level of sensitivity, educational, family and cultural background, financial position, social status, customs, traditions, religious beliefs, human values and their value system as observed by the Apex Court in Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh.

legal_principles.principle: In matrimonial cases, it is not possible in every case to pinpoint to an act of 'cruelty' or blameworthy conduct of the spouse.
